hints: Look closely at the two groups that are facing each other in the box in each diagram. One should come from a carboxyl group (-COOH) and one from an amino group (-NH2).
Remember a peptide bond is a C-N bond made by condensation. An -OH is lost from the carboxyl group and an -H is lost from the amino group to make water, H2O.
walkthrough:
**Recall what an amino acid looks like**

Every amino acid has the same backbone. There is a central carbon with an amino group ($-NH_2$) on one side and a carboxyl group ($-COOH$) on the other side.

To make a peptide bond, these two different ends must meet.

**Recall how a peptide bond forms**

It is a condensation reaction. The -OH is removed from the carboxyl group of one amino acid, and one -H is removed from the amino group of the next amino acid.

$$-COOH + H_2N- \rightarrow -CO-NH- + H_2O$$
The new $C-N$ link left behind is the peptide bond.

**Check where the box is taking atoms from**

Only diagram A boxes an -OH from a $C-OH$ (carboxyl end) and an -H from an $N-H$ (amino end). Removing those leaves C and N free to join directly.

That is exactly where water is lost and where the peptide bond will form, so A is correct.

options.A: Correct. The box contains OH from the carboxyl group on the left and H from the amino group on the right. Loss of H2O here leaves a C-N peptide bond.
options.B: False. The box joins two carboxyl ends together (C-O-C type link), not a carboxyl to an amino group, so no C-N peptide bond can form.
options.C: False. The box takes the carbonyl oxygen (C=O) instead of the hydroxyl (C-OH), plus two H from nitrogen. That is the wrong combination for water formation.
options.D: False. Although OH from the carboxyl is boxed, the H is taken from the alpha carbon (C-R), not from the amino group, so a peptide bond cannot form there.
